skill.name: paper-2-web
skill.description: Convert academic papers into research websites, presentation videos, and conference posters using Paper2All workflows for LaTeX or PDF sources.
skill.summary: Guides Paper2All workflows for websites, videos, and posters from academic papers.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: High-severity confirmed findings are mainly credential handling and sudo-based system package installation, not direct malicious code. Most SKILL.md external-command findings are false positives from Markdown code fences or inline command examples. No prompt injection text was found, but the workflow depends on unpinned third-party code and optional external logo search.

remediation.issue: Sudo package installation in community documentation
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a container, documented manual prerequisites, or explicit user confirmation before any elevated package installation.
Document .env file permissions, warn users never to commit it, and recommend least-privilege keys or a local secret manager.
Pin Paper2All to a reviewed commit or release and provide checksum or lockfile verification for dependencies.

remediation.issue: Automatic logo search can call external services
remediation.suggestion: Keep logo search disabled by default, require explicit consent, and validate downloaded image sources before use.

remediation.issue: Executable Bash examples appear throughout the skill
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as manual examples and require confirmation before running clone, install, batch, or generation commands.

content.user_title: Transform Papers Into Research Websites and Media
content.value_statement: Academic papers are hard to share beyond static PDFs. This skill guides Paper2All workflows for websites, posters, and videos from LaTeX or PDF inputs.
actual_capabilities: Guides Paper2Web generation of responsive academic homepages from LaTeX or PDF inputs.
Provides Paper2Video workflows for narrated presentation videos and optional talking-head output.
Provides Paper2Poster workflows for print-ready conference posters with custom dimensions.
Documents installation, API key setup, model selection, and system dependencies.
Supports single-paper and batch workflows with branding and multi-language options.
Lists quality checks for websites, posters, videos, accessibility, and print readiness.
limitations: The skill does not include the Paper2All pipeline code.
Generation may require paid LLM APIs and local API key configuration.
Talking-head videos require a high-memory NVIDIA GPU.
Scientific accuracy, citations, accessibility, and print quality still need human review.

use_cases.title: Create a Paper Homepage
use_cases.description: Turn a completed paper into a responsive website with figures, results, citations, and author information.

use_cases.title: Prepare Conference Materials
use_cases.description: Generate a poster, short video abstract, and companion website for a conference submission.

use_cases.title: Publish Lab Research Assets
use_cases.description: Plan consistent websites, posters, and videos for several papers from one lab or project group.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to turn my paper folder into an interactive research website. Ask for any missing inputs before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Conference Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to plan a website, poster, and short video for my conference paper. Include required inputs and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Generation Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to check whether my LaTeX or PDF source is ready for Paper2All generation. Report missing files and risks.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to design a batch workflow for several papers. Prioritize websites first, then posters, then videos, with QA for each output.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for an interactive homepage from a LaTeX paper.
output: A Paper2Web workflow with required input files and output folders.
A website plan covering abstract, methods, results, figures, citations, and author details.
A review checklist for responsive layout, working links, and figure quality.

output_examples.input: A conference presenter needs a poster and short video.
output: A production plan for poster size, visual hierarchy, narration length, and branding.
A list of assets needed before generation, including figures and bibliography files.
Review steps for print readability, audio synchronization, and scientific accuracy.

output_examples.input: A lab wants dissemination assets for several accepted papers.
output: A batch approach with one output folder per paper.
A priority order that creates websites first, then posters, then videos.
A final review checklist for content accuracy, branding, and publication readiness.

best_practices: Use clean LaTeX sources with complete figures, tables, and bibliography files.
Review generated claims, citations, links, accessibility, and figure quality before publishing.
Keep API keys outside version control and run generation in an isolated environment.
anti_patterns: Running installation commands in a production environment without isolation or confirmation.
Publishing generated materials without checking scientific accuracy and author approvals.
Enabling external logo search without verifying licensing, sources, and downloaded assets.

faq.question: Does this skill generate the website by itself?
faq.answer: It guides Paper2All workflows and may run approved commands. The external Paper2All project performs the generation.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Clean LaTeX with figures, tables, and bibliography works best. High-quality PDFs can also be used.

faq.question: Are API keys required?
faq.answer: Most LLM-powered generation requires OpenAI, OpenRouter, or Google API keys. Store keys securely and avoid committing them.

faq.question: Can it create posters and videos too?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers Paper2Web, Paper2Poster, and Paper2Video workflows from the same research source.

faq.question: Can I use only a PDF?
faq.answer: Yes, but selectable text and high-resolution figures improve extraction quality. LaTeX usually gives better structure.

faq.question: What security precautions should I use?
faq.answer: Use an isolated environment, review commands before execution, pin trusted sources, and protect the .env file.
